name: Level Goal
description: The end of the level: a region that, once the player reaches it, means they finished. It fires once by default, because a goal that re-fires every frame the player stands in it turns a completion into a stutter of completions. It reports the elapsed time with the event, which is the one number a level's ending is almost always asked for. progression.levelCompleted carries both the `notify` and `persist` intents — finishing is worth telling the player about and worth writing down, and a build with a toast and a save gets both without either being wired to this.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: region
inputs.description: The goal rectangle in world units, {x, y, width, height}. Required with no default: a level whose goal is at the origin is not a level.

inputs.name: completeOnce
inputs.description: Whether reaching the goal can fire more than once. False suits a lap or a checkpoint reused as a goal; true is what a level ending means.

inputs.name: label
inputs.description: What the goal is called, carried on the event so a toast can say something better than 'levelCompleted'.

outputs.name: elapsedSeconds
outputs.description: Time since the component was constructed, stopped at completion. This is the level's clock.
